name: Chin filler

lead: Chin filler is a non-surgical way to add volume to the chin, most often with hyaluronic acid gel injected by a clinician. Companies have run registered trials of several products specifically for chin retrusion, and published case reviews describe its use for reshaping the facial profile.

On looksmax.org it is discussed as a trial run before surgery or a temporary alternative to implants and genioplasty. Forum members also post self-injection accounts, which clinicians regard as outside normal safety conditions.

paras: Hyaluronic acid or similar gel is injected near the bone to add volume, projecting or lengthening the chin. The effect lasts as long as the material persists in the tissue and is reversible with hyaluronidase for hyaluronic acid products.

The chin is generally regarded as a lower-risk injection area, but case reports describe vascular occlusion, skin necrosis and even tongue necrosis after chin filler. Anatomical studies map the arteries to inform safer injection. Fillers are regulated medical devices administered by licensed practitioners.

lead: Chin filler is a non-surgical cosmetic treatment in which an injectable gel, typically hyaluronic acid, is placed in the chin to increase its projection, height or contour. It is sometimes called a liquid genioplasty and is used both for age-related volume loss and for congenital chin retrusion. [1][2]

Published work includes a case review of 83 patients treated with combined forehead, nose and chin filler to alter the profile [1], and manufacturers have registered several trials of specific hyaluronic acid products for chin retrusion. [3][4][5] The literature also documents rare serious complications, including vascular occlusion and tongue necrosis. [6][7]

In looksmaxxing communities chin filler is discussed as a reversible, lower-cost alternative or precursor to chin implants and sliding genioplasty. Forum members also post accounts of self-injection; clinical literature on safety concerns the anatomy and complications of professional injection. [2][8][9]
infobox: Chin implant, sliding genioplasty, fat grafting

paras: The filler is deposited in or near the chin's soft tissue and over the bone to move the soft-tissue pogonion forward or lengthen the chin. An encyclopedic summary of chin surgery lists hyaluronic acid and calcium hydroxyapatite as temporary fillers and notes that permanent silicone fillers have fallen out of favour because of migration and infection risks. [10]
A published technique paper describes a multilayered cannula approach to the chin, and a case series proposes a profile algorithm combining forehead, nose, lip and chin filler. [1][11]
A study using three-dimensional tomography and cadaveric dissection of 40 heads examined chin anatomy to discuss the avoidance of intravascular embolization. [2]

A case series reported unilateral tongue necrosis from vascular occlusion after hyaluronic acid chin augmentation, stating that chin filler is considered a safe injection area and that this complication is rare. [6] A 2026 case report describes vascular occlusion after a low-volume chin injection managed with pulsed hyaluronidase. [7]

Forum members ask whether chin filler would improve their profile, post transformation photographs, and discuss it alongside jaw filler. [8][9][12] Some threads document members injecting themselves or friends [13]; the wiki does not reproduce such instructions, and published literature on complications concerns professional administration. [6][2]
A case review of 83 consecutive patients treated with forehead, nose and chin filler assessed profile measurements and complications. [1]

Registered trials for chin products include Restylane Lyft with lidocaine (NCT05777759, n=175), Restylane Defyne (NCT03624816, n=140), a new dermal filler for chin correction (NCT04631263, n=140), Stylage XXL in Chinese adults (NCT05009381, n=174), Restylane Shaype versus Juvederm Volux (NCT06336772, n=40), and a phase 4 evaluation recruiting in 2026 (NCT07777926). [3][4][5][14][15][16]

lore.intro: Members of looksmax.org discuss chin filler as a temporary, reversible way to test or improve chin projection, and some post self-injection results. [8][9][12]
